profile.address: Booneville Road, West Des Moines, Boone Township, Dallas County, Iowa, 50266
profile.reading: This building is part of Microsoft's West Des Moines, Iowa data center hub, a cluster of campuses the company has built since first opening in the city in 2012. Microsoft has invested an estimated $5 billion to $6 billion across its West Des Moines facilities to date, per reporting from Wisconsin Public Radio, which visited the site while researching a comparable Microsoft project in Wisconsin, and the company now owns more than 600 acres across the metro. West Des Moines' city engineer told WPR that each Microsoft campus typically comprises three to four buildings and takes roughly eight to ten years to fully build out, which is consistent with this registry finding multiple OSM-mapped Microsoft buildings clustered along the same streets in Dallas, Polk, and Warren counties. More than 600 people now work across Microsoft's West Des Moines data centers, in roles spanning mechanical and electrical engineering, campus management, IT operations, security, and building maintenance, making Microsoft roughly the seventh- or eighth-largest full-time employer in a city of about 73,000 residents. One of the named campuses, internally called Project Osmium, sits on the south side of West Des Moines near Interstate 35; the Business Record has separately reported on a sixth Microsoft data center project, called Project Ruthenium, planned near Veterans Parkway and Woodland Avenue with an initial $210 million, 245,000-square-foot building and roughly 25 permanent jobs, part of a site that could eventually hold up to four buildings. This building sits along Grand Avenue or Booneville Road in Dallas County, in the western portion of Microsoft's West Des Moines footprint; Microsoft has not published which named campus or project this specific building belongs to, nor its individual square footage or MW capacity, consistent with the company's general practice of not disclosing per-building specifics for its Azure data centers.

reading.body:
Microsoft's West Des Moines campus in Dallas County is part of a multi-county complex where the operator has invested $1.5 to $2 billion and plans a sixth data center building, but Microsoft publishes no individual campus power capacity, square footage, or building-level specifications. The operator discloses only aggregate worldwide statistics: 500+ data centers across 80+ Azure regions drawing on 40+ gigawatts of contracted renewable energy, which means individual facility figures remain unknown. Without published capacity for this site, its scale in the AI infrastructure stack cannot be read from operator disclosure.

Among Iowa's 52 mapped data center facilities, only two operators publish power figures, totaling 18 megawatts across the state. This campus ranks third by published megawatts in Iowa, though that ranking reflects the absence of published data for 50 other mapped facilities statewide, not confirmed capacity at this location. Iowa's published footprint is negligible in national AI scaling; the state's two disclosed facilities represent a rounding error against gigawatt-scale campuses in other regions.

The campus matters to infrastructure investors and grid planners because Microsoft's reported $1.5 to $2 billion commitment and plans for continued expansion signal sustained demand for Iowa power and real estate. The actual demand this campus places on the Iowa grid, and whether it rivals or dwarfs other undisclosed facilities statewide, remains opaque by the operator's policy and therefore cannot be weighed against grid constraints from published facts alone.
